title: Vertical rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and set the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. Begin by drawing a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In the first loop, draw the first line from the origin at zero, zero to zero point one two seven seven, zero. Draw the second line from zero point one two seven seven, zero to zero point one two seven seven, zero point seven five. Draw the third line from zero point one two seven seven, zero point seven five to zero, zero point seven five. Finally, draw the fourth line from zero, zero point seven five back to the origin at zero, zero. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point seven five. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using the Euler angles negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and translating it using the translation vector zero, zero, and zero. Extrude the transformed sketch along the normal direction by zero point zero one six units to create a new solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. The dimensions of the resulting vertical rectangular prism are zero point one two seven six five nine five seven four four six eight zero eight five one units in length, zero point seven four nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine units in width, and zero point zero one five nine five seven four four six eight zero eight five one zero six three seven units in height. This completes the construction of the first part, forming the base of the vertical rectangular prism with a flat top and bottom.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1277, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1277, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.016)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r = r

# Display the model

lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# The part is a simple rectangular plate.
# Dimensions from the bounding box:
#   X (thickness) = 0.0160
#   Y (depth)     = 0.1277
#   Z (height)    = 0.7500

plate_thickness = 0.0160
plate_depth = 0.1277
plate_height = 0.7500

# Build the plate: sketch the Y-Z profile on the YZ plane,
# then extrude along +X by the thickness.
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .rect(plate_depth, plate_height)
    .extrude(plate_thickness)
)

# Assign the final solid to variable r
